chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan b. Ali b. Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from his father Ali b. Yaqtin. He said:

The news was brought to Musa b. Ja'far (peace be upon them both), while he was with a group of his household, about what Musa b. al-Mahdi had resolved regarding his affair. He said to his household: What do you advise? They said: We think that you should distance yourself from this man and hide yourself from him, for indeed his evil cannot be trusted. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) smiled and then said: Sakhina claimed she would overcome her Lord, but surely the one who contends with the All-Conquering will be overcome. Then he (peace be upon him) raised his hand to the sky and said:

My God, how many an enemy has sharpened for me the blade of his knife, and honed for me the tip of his blade, and mixed for me deadly poisons, while the eye of his watch did not sleep concerning me. When You saw my weakness in bearing calamities and my inability against the onslaught of disasters, You diverted that from me by Your ability and Your power, not by my ability nor my power. You threw him into the pit he had dug for me, disappointed from what he hoped for in his worldly life, far removed from what he hoped for in his Hereafter. So to You is praise for that, as much as You deserve. My Master, O Allah, seize him by Your might, and blunt his blade against me by Your power. Make for him preoccupation in what concerns him and inability against whoever opposes him. O Allah, assist me against him with a present assault that may be a remedy for my rage and a fulfillment of my right against him. O Allah, connect my supplication with acceptance and rearrange my complaints with change. Acquaint him soon with what You have promised the oppressors, and acquaint me with what You have promised in answering the desperate. Surely You are possessor of great grace and noble beneficence.
He said: Then the people dispersed, and they did not gather again except for reading the letter that arrived with the death of Musa b. al-Mahdi.

key_terms.أبو الحسن: Abu al-Hasan — kunya of Imam Musa al-Kadhim
key_terms.الحفير: the pit — metaphor for the trap an enemy sets that becomes his own downfall
key_terms.المضطرين: the desperate — those in dire need who call upon God (cf. Quran 27:62)
key_terms.سخينة: Sakhina — poetic name for Quraysh, from a poem of Ka'b b. Malik
key_terms.موسى بن المهدي: Musa b. al-Mahdi — brother of Harun al-Rashid who plotted against the Imam

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Musa al-Kadhim make when threatened by Musa b. al-Mahdi?
ai.summary: Ali b. Yaqtin reports that when Imam Musa al-Kadhim learned of Musa b. al-Mahdi's plot against him, his family advised him to flee. Instead, the Imam smiled, recited a poem expressing trust in God's victory, then raised his hands and made a powerful supplication asking God to protect him by His power alone. The Imam's prayer was answered shortly after, as Musa b. al-Mahdi died before he could carry out his plot.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from his father `Ali b. Yaqtin. He said:

The news came to Musa b. Ja`far (as) while he was with a group of his family that a plot by Musa b. al-Mahdi (the brother of Harun al-Rashid) was made against him. So, he said to his family: What do you think? They said: We believe that you should avoid this man and that you should hide yourself from him, for one cannot be safe from his evil. So, Abu’l Hasan (as) smiled and recited [a poem of Ka`b b. Malik]: Sakhina (Quraysh) thought that she could defeat her master, but the victors can be defeated. Then, he (as) raised his hand to the sky and said:

My God! How many enemies sharpen their daggers for me, and pour deadly poison for me, with no eye sleeping away from me, watching? When You saw my weakness in withstanding calamity and my inability to act in poverty, You diverted all that from me by Your ability and Your power, not by my ability nor my power. You threw them in the ditch that they had dug out for me, as they are let down from what they hoped for in this world and are divergent from what they hoped for in the Hereafter. So, praise be to You – as much as You have the right to it – for this [blessing]. My Master, O Allah! Seize him, by Your glory, and make his dagger against me dull, by Your power. Make him busy running his own affairs and incapacitate him against his enemies. O Allah! Assist me against him now, so that it may be a remedy for my rage, and so that it may be a fulfillment of my right against him. O Allah! Connect my prayer with its acceptance and rearrange my complaints to [You] with change. Acquaint him with some of what You have promised the oppressors and acquaint me with the answer that You have promised the desperate. Surely, You are of great nobility and of benevolent blessing.
He said: Then, he split away from the people. They were not reunited until the obituary of Musa b. al-Mahdi was read out [soon after that].
